questions.text: कोशिकाओं के निम्नलिखित समूहों में से कौन-सा समूह नर जनन-ग्रंथि (गोनड) में अगुणित कोशिकाओं का निरूपण करता है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following groups of cells in the male gonad represent haploid cells?
questions.solution: Secondary spermatocytes (option C) are haploid cells because they are formed after the completion of Meiosis I, which reduces the chromosome number from diploid (2n) to haploid (n). Spermatogonial cells and germinal epithelial cells are diploid (2n). Primary spermatocytes are also diploid as they undergo Meiosis I but have not yet completed it.
questions.solution_hindi: द्वितीयक शुक्राणुकोशिकाएँ (विकल्प C) अगुणित होती हैं क्योंकि वे अर्धसूत्री विभाजन I की समाप्ति के बाद बनती हैं, जिससे गुणसूत्र संख्या द्विगुणित (2n) से अगुणित (n) हो जाती है। शुक्राणुजनीय कोशिकाएँ और जनन उपकला कोशिकाएँ द्विगुणित (2n) होती हैं। प्राथमिक शुक्राणुकोशिकाएँ भी द्विगुणित होती हैं क्योंकि वे अर्धसूत्री विभाजन I से गुजर रही होती हैं।

questions.text: एक आवृतबीजी (ऐंजियोस्पर्म) के भ्रूणकोश में तंतुरूप उपकरण बीजांडद्वारीय सिरे (छोर) पर उपस्थित कोशिकाओं के सिरे पर पाया जाता है:
questions.text_english: Filiform apparatus in the embryo sac of an angiosperm is present at the micropylar tip of:
questions.solution: The filiform apparatus is found at the micropylar tip of the synergids (option C). Synergids are two cells flanking the egg cell in the embryo sac. The filiform apparatus helps in directing and absorbing the pollen tube, facilitating the entry of male gametes toward the egg cell. The central cell, egg cell, and antipodals do not possess this structure.
questions.solution_hindi: तंतुरूप उपकरण सहाय कोशिकाओं (विकल्प C) के बीजांडद्वारीय सिरे पर पाया जाता है। सहाय कोशिकाएँ भ्रूणकोश में अंड कोशिका के दोनों ओर स्थित दो कोशिकाएँ हैं। यह उपकरण परागनली को निर्देशित करने में और नर युग्मकों को अंड कोशिका तक पहुँचाने में सहायता करता है।

questions.text:
एक व्यक्ति के वीर्य में शुक्राणुओं की गणना 20 मिलियन/मिली (mL) से कम है तथा उसकी पत्नी की अंडवाहिनी अवरोधित पाई गई है। इस दंपत्ति (युगल) को उपचार हेतु निम्नलिखित में से किस तकनीक को अपनाने की सलाह दी जा सकती है?
(i) जेडआईएफटी
(ii) एआई
(iii) आईयूटी
(iv) आईसीएसआई
(v) जीआईएफटी
questions.text_english:
A man is found to have a sperm count of less than 20 million/mL and his wife is diagnosed with blockage in the oviduct. This couple would be advised to go for which of the following techniques?
(i) ZIFT
(ii) AI
(iii) IUT
(iv) ICSI
(v) GIFT
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) — IUT and ICSI. Since the man has a low sperm count (oligospermia), ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection) is suitable, where a single sperm is directly injected into the egg. Since the wife's oviduct is blocked, in vitro fertilisation is required and the zygote/embryo must be transferred directly into the uterus using IUT (Intra-Uterine Transfer). ZIFT involves transfer into the fallopian tube, which is blocked here. AI requires normal sperm count. GIFT transfers gametes into the fallopian tube, which is also not feasible here.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) — आईयूटी और आईसीएसआई है। पुरुष में शुक्राणु संख्या कम है, अतः आईसीएसआई उपयुक्त है जिसमें एकल शुक्राणु को सीधे अंड में इंजेक्ट किया जाता है। पत्नी की अंडवाहिनी अवरुद्ध है, इसलिए भ्रूण को सीधे गर्भाशय में स्थानांतरित करने के लिए आईयूटी उपयोगी है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित ऐमीनो अम्ल प्रतिस्थापन में से कौन-सा विकल्प दात्र कोशिका अरक्तता (सिकल सेल एनीमिया) विकार (रोग) के लिए उत्तरदायी है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following amino acid substitutions is responsible for causing sickle cell anemia?

options.A: β-ग्लोबिन श्रृंखला के छठे स्थान पर अवस्थित वेलीन का प्रतिस्थापन ग्लूटैमिक अम्ल द्वारा होता है।
options.B: β-ग्लोबिन श्रृंखला के सातवें स्थान पर अवस्थित वेलीन का प्रतिस्थापन ग्लूटैमिक अम्ल द्वारा होता है।
options.C: β-ग्लोबिन श्रृंखला के छठे स्थान पर अवस्थित ग्लूटैमिक अम्ल का प्रतिस्थापन वेलीन द्वारा होता है।
options.D: α-ग्लोबिन श्रृंखला के छठे स्थान पर अवस्थित ग्लूटैमिक अम्ल का प्रतिस्थापन वेलीन द्वारा होता है।

options_english.A: Valine is substituted by glutamic acid in the β-globin chain at the sixth position.
options_english.B: Valine is substituted by glutamic acid in the β-globin chain at the seventh position.
options_english.C: Glutamic acid is substituted by valine in the β-globin chain at the sixth position.
options_english.D: Glutamic acid is substituted by valine in the α-globin chain at the sixth position.

questions.solution: Sickle cell anemia is caused by a point mutation in the β-globin gene where glutamic acid (a hydrophilic amino acid) at the sixth position of the β-globin chain is substituted by valine (a hydrophobic amino acid), as stated in option C. This change alters the shape of the haemoglobin molecule under low oxygen conditions, causing red blood cells to become sickle-shaped. Option A and B are incorrect because the direction of substitution is reversed. Option D is incorrect because it is the β-globin chain, not the α-globin chain, that is affected.
questions.solution_hindi: सिकल सेल एनीमिया β-ग्लोबिन जीन में बिंदु उत्परिवर्तन के कारण होता है जिसमें β-ग्लोबिन श्रृंखला के छठे स्थान पर ग्लूटैमिक अम्ल का प्रतिस्थापन वेलीन द्वारा होता है। यही विकल्प C में कहा गया है। इस परिवर्तन से कम ऑक्सीजन की स्थिति में हीमोग्लोबिन अणु का आकार बदल जाता है और लाल रक्त कोशिकाएँ हँसिए जैसी हो जाती हैं।

questions.text: मानव के विलुप्त पूर्वज का नाम बताइए जो केवल फल खाते थे तथा पत्थर के हथियारों से शिकार करते थे।
questions.text_english: Name the extinct ancestor of humans who ate only fruits and hunted with stone weapons.
questions.solution: Australopithecus (option B) is the correct answer. Australopithecus was an early hominid that lived in Africa and primarily ate fruits. They were also known to hunt with primitive stone weapons. Ramapithecus was more ape-like and ate hard seeds and nuts. Dryopithecus was mostly ape-like and ate forest fruits. Homo erectus used fire, ate meat, and had a larger brain — they are not described as eating only fruits.
questions.solution_hindi: ऑस्ट्रेलोपिथेकस (विकल्प B) सही उत्तर है। यह एक आरंभिक होमिनिड था जो मुख्यतः फल खाता था और पत्थर के हथियारों का उपयोग करता था। रामापिथेकस वानर जैसा था और कठोर बीज खाता था। ड्रायोपिथेकस वनों में रहता और फल खाता था। होमो इरेक्टस आग का उपयोग करता था और मांस खाता था।

questions.text:
सही कथनों का चयन कीजिए:
(i) बहुसिस्ट्रॉनिक (पॉलीसिस्ट्रॉनिक) एमआरएनए सामान्यतः सुकेन्द्रकियों में पाया जाता है।
(ii) आरएनए पॉलीमरेज II एमआरएनए के पूर्ववर्ती, एचएनआरएनए (hnRNA) का अनुलेखन करता है।
(iii) जब दूत-आरएनए (एमआरएनए) राइबोसोम की बड़ी उपएकक के साथ एकीकृत होता है तब एमआरएनए का स्थानांतरण (रूपांतरण) प्रक्रम प्रारंभ होता है।
(iv) रोध प्रकूट (स्टॉप कोडॉन) में कोई टी-आरएनए नहीं होता है।
questions.text_english:
Choose the correct statements:
(i) Polycistronic mRNA is generally found in eukaryotes.
(ii) The RNA polymerase II transcribes precursor of mRNA, the hnRNA.
(iii) The process of translation of mRNA begins when the mRNA encounters the large subunit of ribosomes.
(iv) Stop codons do not have any tRNAs.
questions.solution: Option C — statements (ii) and (iv) are correct. RNA polymerase II is indeed responsible for transcribing hnRNA, which is the precursor of mRNA in eukaryotes. Stop codons (UAA, UAG, UGA) do not have corresponding tRNAs; instead, release factors recognize them to terminate translation. Statement (i) is wrong because polycistronic mRNA is found in prokaryotes, not eukaryotes. Statement (iii) is wrong because translation begins when mRNA associates with the small (not large) subunit of the ribosome.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C — कथन (ii) और (iv) सही हैं। आरएनए पॉलीमरेज II hnRNA का अनुलेखन करता है जो सुकेन्द्रकियों में एमआरएनए का पूर्ववर्ती है। स्टॉप कोडॉन (UAA, UAG, UGA) के लिए कोई tRNA नहीं होता। कथन (i) गलत है क्योंकि पॉलीसिस्ट्रॉनिक mRNA अधिकेन्द्रकियों (प्रोकेरियोट्स) में पाया जाता है। कथन (iii) गलत है क्योंकि अनुवाद छोटी (large नहीं) उपएकक से प्रारंभ होता है।

questions.text: जलीय तथा स्थलीय पर्यावरण में नाइट्रोजन का स्थिरीकरण करके मृदा को समृद्ध बनाने वाले कुछ सायनोबैक्टीरिया हैं:
questions.text_english: Some cyanobacteria in aquatic and terrestrial environment that enrich the soil by fixing nitrogen are:
questions.solution: Anabaena and Nostoc (option C) are cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) that fix atmospheric nitrogen both in aquatic and terrestrial environments, thereby enriching the soil. Rhizobium and Azotobacter are bacteria but not cyanobacteria. Azospirillum is a nitrogen-fixing bacterium but not a cyanobacterium. Glomus is a mycorrhizal fungus, not a cyanobacterium.
questions.solution_hindi: ऐनाबीना और नोस्टॉक (विकल्प C) सायनोबैक्टीरिया (नीले-हरे शैवाल) हैं जो जलीय और स्थलीय दोनों वातावरणों में वायुमंडलीय नाइट्रोजन का स्थिरीकरण करते हैं और मृदा को समृद्ध करते हैं। राइजोबियम और ऐजोटोबैक्टर जीवाणु हैं लेकिन सायनोबैक्टीरिया नहीं। ग्लोमस एक कवक है।

questions.text:
निकोटीन रक्तचाप (दाब) तथा हृदय स्पंदन दर को प्रभावित करता है जिसका कारण कुछ विशिष्ट अधिवृक्क हॉर्मोनों का मोचन (स्रावित) होना है। कुछ अधिवृक्क हॉर्मोन निम्नलिखित हैं:
(i) ऐड्रिनेलीन
(ii) कॉर्टिसॉल
(iii) नॉर-ऐड्रिनेलीन
(iv) ऐल्डोस्टेरोन
questions.text_english:
Nicotine affects blood pressure and heart rate due to release of certain adrenal hormones. Following are some of the adrenal hormones:
(i) Adrenaline
(ii) Cortisol
(iii) Noradrenaline
(iv) Aldosterone
questions.solution: Nicotine stimulates the adrenal medulla to release adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine), which are catecholamines that directly increase heart rate and blood pressure. These are the hormones responsible for the 'fight or flight' response. Cortisol is a glucocorticoid from the adrenal cortex and is not directly responsible for acute changes in heart rate. Aldosterone regulates sodium/water balance and does not directly affect heart rate in response to nicotine.
questions.solution_hindi: निकोटीन अधिवृक्क मज्जा को ऐड्रिनेलीन और नॉर-ऐड्रिनेलीन स्रावित करने के लिए उत्तेजित करता है। ये दोनों हॉर्मोन सीधे हृदय स्पंदन दर और रक्तचाप बढ़ाते हैं। कॉर्टिसॉल और ऐल्डोस्टेरोन अधिवृक्क वल्कुट से स्रावित होते हैं और निकोटीन द्वारा प्रत्यक्ष रूप से प्रभावित नहीं होते।

questions.text: क्षालन (इलूशन) का अर्थ है:
questions.text_english: Elution means:

options.A: डीएनए की परतों को पराबैंगनी (UV) विकिरणों की सहायता से देखने योग्य बनाना।
options.B: ऐगारोज जेल पर डीएनए खंडों को पृथक करना।
options.C: चयनित जीव से विजातीय डीएनए को पृथक (विलग) करना।
options.D: ऐगारोज जेल से डीएनए की परतों को काटना तथा निष्कर्षित करना।

options_english.A: Making the DNA bands visible under UV radiations.
options_english.B: Separation of DNA fragments on agarose gel.
options_english.C: Isolating alien DNA from the choice organism.
options_english.D: Cutting and extraction of DNA bands from the agarose gel.

questions.solution: Elution (option D) refers to the process of cutting out the specific DNA band from the agarose gel after it has been visualised under UV light and then extracting (eluting) the DNA from the gel piece. This step is essential in recombinant DNA technology to isolate the desired DNA fragment. Option A describes visualisation, not elution. Option B describes electrophoresis. Option C describes isolation of alien DNA, which is a different step.
questions.solution_hindi: क्षालन (इलूशन) (विकल्प D) का अर्थ है UV प्रकाश में दृश्यमान DNA बैंड को ऐगारोज जेल से काटना और उस जेल के टुकड़े से DNA को निष्कर्षित करना। यह पुनर्संयोजी DNA प्रौद्योगिकी में वांछित DNA खंड को अलग करने के लिए आवश्यक चरण है।

questions.text: पारजीनी जन्तुओं से प्राप्त पुनर्योगज प्रोटीन जिसका उपयोग एम्फीसीमा के उपचार में किया जा सकता है:
questions.text_english: The recombinant protein obtained from transgenic animals that could be used to treat emphysema is:
questions.solution: Alpha-1-antitrypsin (option C) is a recombinant protein obtained from transgenic sheep (Rosie) that is used to treat emphysema, a condition where the alveoli of the lungs are damaged due to deficiency of this protease inhibitor. Humulin is recombinant insulin used for diabetes. α-lactalbumin is a protein found in human milk produced by transgenic cows. Iodothyronine is a thyroid hormone and is not a recombinant protein from transgenic animals for emphysema treatment.
questions.solution_hindi: α-1-ऐंटीट्रिप्सिन (विकल्प C) एक पुनर्योगज प्रोटीन है जो पारजीनी भेड़ (रोज़ी) से प्राप्त होता है और एम्फीसीमा के उपचार में उपयोग किया जाता है। एम्फीसीमा में फेफड़ों की वायुकोशिकाएँ नष्ट हो जाती हैं क्योंकि इस प्रोटीएज अवरोधक की कमी होती है। ह्यूमुलिन मधुमेह के लिए है और α-लैक्टएल्बुमिन एक दुग्ध प्रोटीन है।

questions.text: सर्वप्रथम पुनर्योगज डीएनए का निर्माण जिस जीव के मूल प्लैस्मिड के उपयोग द्वारा किया गया, वह है:
questions.text_english: The construction of the first recombinant DNA was done by using the native plasmid of:
questions.solution: The first recombinant DNA was constructed by Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer in 1972 using the native plasmid of Salmonella typhimurium (option B). They linked the antibiotic resistance gene from one plasmid to another using restriction enzymes and ligase. E. coli is a commonly used host organism but its plasmid was not used for the first rDNA construction. Agrobacterium's Ti plasmid is used for plant transformation, and B. thuringiensis is an insecticidal bacterium.
questions.solution_hindi: पहला पुनर्योगज DNA स्टेनली कोहेन और हर्बर्ट बॉयर ने 1972 में सालमोनेला टाइफीम्यूरियम (विकल्प B) के मूल प्लैस्मिड का उपयोग करके बनाया था। उन्होंने एक प्लैस्मिड से एंटीबायोटिक प्रतिरोध जीन को प्रतिबंध एंजाइम और लाइगेज की मदद से दूसरे प्लैस्मिड से जोड़ा था।

questions.text: कॉनेल के परिष्कृत क्षेत्र के प्रयोगों में पाया गया कि स्कॉटलैंड के चट्टानी समुद्र तटों पर बड़े बार्नेकल बैलेनस का अंतरज्वारीय क्षेत्र में प्रभुत्व था तथा इसने छोटे बार्नेकल चैथेमैलस को उस क्षेत्र से बाहर निकाल दिया। इसका कारण था:
questions.text_english: Connell's elegant field experiments on the rocky seacoast of Scotland, found that larger barnacles Balanus dominated the intertidal area and removed the smaller barnacles Chathamalus. This happened due to:
questions.solution: This is a classic example of interspecific competition (option D). Balanus, being larger and more aggressive, outcompeted the smaller Chathamalus for space and resources in the intertidal zone, excluding it from that area. This is not parasitism (no harm-benefit pair), not predation (Balanus did not eat Chathamalus), and not mutualism (no mutual benefit). Connell's experiment demonstrated the concept of competitive exclusion in a natural setting.

questions.solution: (a) Apomictic seeds can be developed by inducing the development of a seed from an unfertilised egg or from diploid nucellus cells without fertilisation. This can occur naturally in some plants or may be induced through genetic manipulation or hybridisation involving certain species that carry genes for apomixis. A laboratory assistant collected three water samples, namely river water, untreated sewage water and secondary effluent discharged from a sewage treatment plant. But the laboratory attendant did not note which was which. The samples were labelled A, B and C and subjected to a BOD test. The BOD values of the three samples A, B and C were recorded as 30 mg/L, 8 mg/L and 400 mg/L respectively.
(a) Which sample of the water is most polluted?
(b) Can you assign the correct label to each, assuming the river water is relatively clean?

key_points: (a) Sample C with BOD 400 mg/L is the most polluted.
(b) C = untreated sewage (400 mg/L), A = river water (30 mg/L), B = secondary effluent from STP (8 mg/L).

questions.solution: (a) Sample C with a BOD value of 400 mg/L is the most polluted, as BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand) is a measure of organic pollution — the higher the BOD, the more polluted the water. (b) Yes, the labels can be assigned correctly. Since river water is relatively clean, it will have a low but not negligible BOD — therefore, Sample A (30 mg/L) is river water. Secondary effluent from a sewage treatment plant has already undergone treatment and will have a very low BOD, so Sample B (8 mg/L) is the secondary effluent. Untreated sewage will have the highest BOD, so Sample C (400 mg/L) is the untreated sewage water.

(a) Biodiversity must be conserved as it plays an important role in many ecosystem services that nature provides. Explain any two ecosystem services.
OR
(b) (i) State, what does 'standing crop' of a trophic level represent.
(ii) List any two ways of measuring the standing crop of a trophic level.

key_points: Ecosystem service 1: Purification of air and water through natural filtration processes.
Ecosystem service 2: Nutrient cycling — recycling of nutrients like nitrogen and carbon through decomposition and biological activity.
OR (b)(i): Standing crop represents the total biomass (or number of individuals) present at a trophic level at a given time.
OR (b)(ii): It can be measured as fresh/dry weight of biomass per unit area, or as the number of organisms per unit area.

questions.solution:
(a) Two important ecosystem services provided by biodiversity are: First, nutrient cycling — biodiversity, especially decomposers and microbes, ensures the recycling of key nutrients such as carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus back into the ecosystem, maintaining soil fertility and productivity. Second, pollination — many plant species depend on insects, birds, and other animals for pollination. This service supports food production and maintains the structure of natural communities. Without biodiversity, these services would be severely disrupted, affecting human welfare and ecosystem stability.

OR
(b)(i) The 'standing crop' of a trophic level represents the total amount of living organic material (biomass) present at that trophic level at a given point in time. (ii) It can be measured by calculating the fresh weight or dry weight of organisms per unit area of the habitat, or alternatively by counting the number of individuals (population density) per unit area.

questions.text_english: Differentiate between wind-pollinated and insect-pollinated flowers. Give an example of each type.

key_points: Wind-pollinated flowers are small, inconspicuous, lack fragrance and nectar, produce large amounts of light pollen, have feathery/large stigmas exposed to air; e.g., maize/corn.
Insect-pollinated flowers are large, colourful, fragrant, produce nectar, have sticky or spiny pollen present in smaller quantities, have enclosed stigmas; e.g., Salvia.

questions.solution: Wind-pollinated flowers (anemophilous) are generally small, dull-coloured, and inconspicuous. They do not produce nectar or fragrance. Their pollen grains are very light, dry, smooth, and produced in enormous quantities to compensate for the randomness of wind. Their stigmas are large, feathery, and often hang outside the flower to trap airborne pollen. Example: Maize (Zea mays). Insect-pollinated flowers (entomophilous) are usually large, brightly coloured, and fragrant to attract insect pollinators. They produce nectar as a reward. Their pollen grains are sticky, spiny, or rough in texture so they adhere to the body of visiting insects. The stigma is generally sticky. Example: Salvia. The key difference lies in the pollinating agent — wind versus insects — which drives all the structural adaptations of the flower.

questions.text_english: Explain the three different ways in which natural selection operates. Explain with the help of graphs.

key_points: Stabilising selection: favours intermediate phenotypes, reduces variation.
Directional selection: shifts the population mean in one direction toward an extreme phenotype.
Disruptive selection: favours both extremes, eliminates intermediate phenotypes, can lead to speciation.

questions.solution: Natural selection operates in three ways: (1) Stabilising Selection — In this mode, individuals with intermediate (average) phenotypes have greater survival and reproductive success than those at either extreme. Over time, this reduces variation and the population becomes more uniform around the mean. For example, human birth weight is subject to stabilising selection — babies of average weight survive best. In the graph, the bell curve becomes narrower and taller. (2) Directional Selection — Here, individuals at one extreme of the phenotypic range are favoured. The population mean shifts progressively towards that extreme over generations. Industrial melanism in Biston betularia (peppered moth) is a classic example. In the graph, the bell curve shifts to one side. (3) Disruptive Selection — This type favours both extremes of the phenotypic range and works against the intermediate forms. Over time, it can lead to the formation of two distinct groups and may eventually result in speciation. In the graph, the original bell curve splits into two distinct peaks.

questions.text_english:
(a) What is primary productivity? Why does it vary in different types of ecosystems?
(b) Why is the assimilation of energy at the herbivore level called secondary productivity?

key_points: Primary productivity is the rate of production of organic matter by producers per unit area per unit time through photosynthesis.
It varies due to differences in light availability, nutrient supply, temperature, water, and the nature of producer organisms.
Energy assimilation at the herbivore level is called secondary productivity because herbivores are the secondary producers — they consume and convert primary production into their own biomass.

questions.solution: (a) Primary productivity is defined as the amount of organic matter (biomass) produced by producers (autotrophs) per unit area per unit time through the process of photosynthesis. It varies across different types of ecosystems because it depends on several abiotic factors such as light intensity, availability of water, temperature, and nutrient concentrations in the soil or water. Tropical rainforests have very high primary productivity due to abundant sunlight and rainfall, while deserts and polar regions have low primary productivity due to water stress and low temperatures respectively. (b) Energy assimilation at the herbivore level is called secondary productivity because herbivores are the primary consumers (secondary producers) in the food chain. They do not produce their own food through photosynthesis; instead, they consume and transform the organic matter produced by the primary producers into their own biomass. Since this production is the second step in the energy conversion chain, it is called secondary productivity.

questions.text_english:
There are many animals, which have become extinct in the wild, but continue to be maintained in zoological parks. Answer the questions that follow:
(a) What type of bio-diversity conservation is observed in this case?
(b) Explain any other two ways which help in this type of conservation.
(c) Besides zoological parks, mention one place that serves this purpose.

key_points: (a) Ex-situ conservation (outside the natural habitat).
(b) Two ways: (i) Cryopreservation of gametes/embryos; (ii) Maintenance in botanical gardens or seed banks.
(c) Botanical gardens / Seed banks / Gene banks.

questions.solution: (a) This scenario represents ex-situ conservation, which means conserving organisms outside their natural habitat. When animals extinct in the wild are maintained in zoological parks, they are being preserved in an artificial, protected environment away from their original ecosystem. (b) Two other ways that support ex-situ conservation are: (i) Cryopreservation — gametes (sperm and egg cells) or embryos of threatened species are preserved at very low temperatures (in liquid nitrogen at –196°C) in gene banks for long periods without loss of viability. (ii) Botanical gardens — these institutions maintain living collections of wild plant species that may be threatened or extinct in their natural habitat, serving as a reserve for conservation and research. (c) Besides zoological parks, seed banks (such as the National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources in India) serve the purpose of ex-situ conservation by storing seeds of wild and cultivated plant species for long-term preservation.

questions.text_english:
(a) How is insulin different from proinsulin?
(b) Explain all the stages of how human insulin is produced through rDNA technology.

key_points: Proinsulin has an extra connecting C-peptide linking the A and B chains; mature insulin lacks this C-peptide.

rDNA steps: (i) Prepare separate genes for A and B chains of insulin; (ii) Insert each into plasmid vectors; (iii) Introduce into E. coli; (iv) E. coli produces A and B chains; (v) Extract chains and combine with disulfide bonds to form functional insulin.

questions.solution: (a) Proinsulin is the inactive precursor of insulin. It has three polypeptide chains: A, B, and an additional connecting peptide called the C-peptide. Mature insulin is formed by enzymatic removal of the C-peptide, leaving only the A and B chains linked by disulfide bonds. Thus, insulin lacks the C-peptide present in proinsulin. (b) The production of human insulin through rDNA technology involves the following stages: First, the DNA sequences encoding the A and B chains of human insulin are chemically synthesised separately. Second, these gene sequences are inserted into separate plasmid vectors (such as pBR322). Third, the recombinant plasmids are introduced into E. coli host cells. Fourth, the bacteria are allowed to grow and express the gene, producing insulin A and B chains separately. Fifth, both polypeptide chains are extracted, purified, and then combined together under controlled conditions to form disulfide bonds between them. The resulting product is active human insulin, marketed as Humulin.

questions.text: (क) मानव शरीर की उन कोशिकाओं के नाम लिखिए जिन पर एचआईवी मानव शरीर में प्रविष्ट होने के उपरान्त सबसे पहले हमला करते हैं। तत्पश्चात् यह विषाणु (वायरस) शरीर में किस प्रकार प्रतिकृतियन करके प्रतिरक्षा न्यूनता (इम्यूनोडिफिसिएंसी) रोग उत्पन्न करता है?
questions.text_english:
(a) Name the cells of the human body attacked by HIV first, when it gains entry into a human body. How does this virus replicate further to cause immunodeficiency in the body?
OR
(b) Show with the help of a flow chart only, the life-cycle of malarial parasite in human.

key_points: HIV first attacks macrophages and T-helper lymphocytes (CD4+ T-cells).
HIV uses reverse transcriptase to make DNA from its RNA genome; this viral DNA integrates into host cell genome and produces new viruses that infect more T-cells.
Massive destruction of T-helper cells leads to immunodeficiency (AIDS), making the patient susceptible to opportunistic infections.

questions.solution:
(a) When HIV enters the human body, it first attacks macrophages and T-helper lymphocytes (CD4+ T-cells). In macrophages, HIV uses its RNA genome as a template and the enzyme reverse transcriptase to produce viral DNA. This viral DNA then integrates into the host cell's chromosome, forming what is called a provirus. The infected macrophages act as a reservoir for HIV and produce new virus particles continuously. HIV then enters the T-helper lymphocytes (T4 cells) in large numbers, replicates, and destroys them. As the number of T-helper cells progressively decreases, the immune system becomes severely compromised. The patient loses the ability to fight off common infections and becomes vulnerable to opportunistic pathogens (such as Pneumocystis jirovecii for pneumonia), ultimately developing AIDS (Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome).

OR
(b) Life cycle of malarial parasite (Plasmodium) in humans:
Infected Anopheles mosquito bites human → Sporozoites enter blood → Sporozoites travel to liver → Liver cells (hepatocytes) infected → Asexual reproduction (schizogony) → Merozoites released → Merozoites infect RBCs → Repeated schizogony in RBCs → RBCs rupture releasing merozoites + toxins (causes fever) → Some merozoites form gametocytes (sexual forms) → Gametocytes ingested by Anopheles mosquito during next bite.

questions.text_english:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:

Immunity in our body is of two types (i) Innate immunity, and (ii) Acquired immunity. Innate immunity is a non-specific defence mechanism, whereas Acquired immunity is pathogen specific. Acquired immunity is characterised by memory. Antibodies are specific to antigens and there are four types of antibodies produced in our body — IgA, IgE, IgG and IgM. It shows primary response where it encounters the pathogen for the first time and secondary response during the subsequent encounters with the same antigen/pathogen. These immune responses are carried out with the help of two special types of lymphocytes present in the blood.

sub_questions.text: उन दो प्रकार की विशिष्ट कोशिकाओं का नाम लिखिए जो प्राथमिक तथा द्वितीयक अनुक्रियाओं को संपादित करती हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the two types of specialised cells which carry out the primary and secondary responses.

key_points: B-lymphocytes (B-cells) and T-lymphocytes (T-cells).

sub_questions.solution: The two types of specialised lymphocytes that carry out the primary and secondary immune responses are B-lymphocytes (B-cells) and T-lymphocytes (T-cells). B-cells are responsible for humoral immunity (antibody production), while T-cells mediate cell-mediated immunity. Memory B-cells and memory T-cells are formed after the primary response and are responsible for the faster and stronger secondary immune response upon re-exposure to the same antigen.

sub_questions.text: हमारे शरीर में उपस्थित किन्हीं दो अवरोधों के नाम लिखिए जो सहज प्रतिरक्षा प्रदान करते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english:
Name any two barriers present in our body that provide innate immunity.
OR
(b)(ii) The organ transplants (grafts) are often rejected if not taken from suitable compatible persons. Mention the characteristic of our immune system that is responsible for the rejection.

key_points: Two barriers: (i) Skin — acts as a physical barrier preventing entry of pathogens; (ii) Mucus lining of the respiratory/digestive tract — traps microorganisms. (OR (b)(ii): The immune system's ability to distinguish self from non-self (immunological recognition / MHC incompatibility) is responsible for graft rejection.)

sub_questions.solution:
Two barriers that provide innate immunity are: (i) Skin — the intact skin acts as the first line of physical defence, preventing the entry of pathogens into the body by acting as an impenetrable barrier. (ii) Mucus — the mucus-secreting epithelium lining the respiratory tract, gastrointestinal tract, and urogenital tract traps foreign particles and microorganisms, preventing them from invading deeper tissues.

OR
(b)(ii): Graft rejection is caused by the immune system's ability to distinguish between 'self' and 'non-self'. This property is based on the Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) — a set of proteins present on the surface of all body cells. If the donor's MHC molecules (HLA antigens) do not match those of the recipient, the recipient's T-cells recognise the graft as foreign and mount an immune attack to destroy it. This is the characteristic responsible for transplant rejection.

sub_questions.text: सक्रिय प्रतिरक्षा (ऐक्टिव इम्युनिटी) निष्क्रिय (पैसिव इम्युनिटी) से किस प्रकार भिन्न है? कोई दो अंतर लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: How is active immunity different from passive immunity? Write any two differences.

key_points: Active immunity is produced by the body's own immune response; passive immunity involves transfer of ready-made antibodies from outside.
Active immunity has long-lasting memory; passive immunity is short-lived and has no immunological memory.

sub_questions.solution: Active immunity is the type of immunity generated when the body's own immune system is stimulated to produce antibodies in response to an antigen (either through natural infection or vaccination). It involves the development of immunological memory and is long-lasting. Passive immunity, on the other hand, is the type of immunity acquired by receiving ready-made antibodies from an external source — for example, injection of antitoxins (such as anti-snake venom) or natural transfer of maternal antibodies to a foetus through the placenta or through colostrum. Passive immunity acts quickly but does not produce immunological memory and is therefore short-lived.

questions.text_english:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:

Gene expresses itself in a cell system as a protein/enzyme. How an expression of gene occurs in a cell system, when it needs to occur and how the gene expression is regulated in prokaryotic cell system was studied by the combined efforts of Francois Jacob, a geneticist and Jacques Monod, a biochemist. For their work on lactose metabolism in E. coli and introducing the concept of 'lac operon', they were awarded the Nobel Prize in 1965.

sub_questions.text: यह कहा गया कि बैक्टीरियल (जीवाणु) कोशिका में 'लैक ऑपेरॉन' बहुत ही कम (अल्प) स्तर पर सदा ही क्रियाशील रहता है। कथन की पुष्टि कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: It is said that 'lac operon' has to be operational at a very low level in the bacterial cell all the time. Justify.

key_points: A basal level of lac operon activity is required to produce a small amount of permease so that if lactose becomes available, it can be transported inside the cell to act as an inducer.

sub_questions.solution: The lac operon must remain operational at a very low basal level at all times because the cell needs to produce a small amount of permease (the enzyme encoded by the lacY gene) continuously. Permease is required to transport lactose from outside the cell into the cytoplasm. Without this minimal level of permease, no lactose can enter the cell, and therefore no inducer would be present to induce the operon further. Thus, the basal level of activity ensures that the cell is always ready to respond when lactose is available in the environment.

sub_questions.text:
ई. कोलाई के लैक ऑपेरॉन में संरचनात्मक जीन किस प्रकार सक्रिय होते हैं?
अथवा
(ख)(ii) इस प्रचालेक (ऑपेरॉन) का नियमन ऋणात्मक नियमन (नेगेटिव रेगुलेशन) क्यों कहलाता है?
sub_questions.text_english:
How are the structural genes activated in the lac operon in E. coli?
OR
(b)(ii) Why is the regulation of operon called negative regulation?

key_points: (i) Structural genes are activated when lactose (the inducer) binds to the repressor protein, causing it to change shape and detach from the operator region, allowing RNA polymerase to transcribe the structural genes.
(ii) It is called negative regulation because in the absence of the inducer (lactose), a repressor protein actively blocks transcription by binding to the operator.

sub_questions.solution:
(b)(i) In E. coli, the lac operon structural genes (lacZ, lacY, lacA) are normally kept switched off because the repressor protein (produced by the regulator gene) binds to the operator region and prevents transcription. When lactose is present in the medium, it acts as an inducer. Allolactose (a metabolite of lactose) binds to the repressor protein and causes a conformational change, making the repressor unable to bind to the operator. The operator is now free, and RNA polymerase can transcribe all three structural genes simultaneously, producing the enzymes needed to metabolise lactose.

OR
(b)(ii) The regulation of the lac operon is called negative regulation because it relies on the action of a repressor protein that actively turns off (negatively regulates) transcription. In the absence of the inducer, the repressor binds to the operator and blocks RNA polymerase, keeping the operon in the 'off' state. The control is 'negative' because the default state is inhibition — the repressor negatively controls gene expression until the inducer removes this block.

sub_questions.text: लैक ऑपेरॉन को अनुलेखनीय नियमित तंत्र क्यों कहा जाता है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is lac operon said to be a transcriptionally regulated system?

key_points: The lac operon is called transcriptionally regulated because control of gene expression occurs at the level of transcription — the repressor controls whether RNA polymerase can access and transcribe the structural genes.
The regulatory mechanism (repressor binding/release from operator) determines when transcription begins or is blocked.

sub_questions.solution: The lac operon is called a transcriptionally regulated system because the control of its gene expression operates at the stage of transcription, not at translation or post-translation. The key regulatory event is the binding or release of the repressor protein from the operator sequence located on the DNA. When the repressor is bound to the operator, it physically prevents RNA polymerase from moving along the DNA and transcribing the structural genes (lacZ, lacY, lacA). When the repressor is removed (by the inducer allolactose), RNA polymerase is free to transcribe the structural genes. Since the entire switch of 'on' and 'off' occurs at the transcription stage, the lac operon is said to be a transcriptionally regulated system.

key_points: EcoR I: 'E' from Escherichia, 'co' from coli, 'R' from strain RY13, 'I' means it was the first enzyme isolated from this strain.

The T-DNA of Ti plasmid integrates into plant cell genome and overproduces cytokinins and auxins, causing uncontrolled cell division leading to tumour (crown gall disease).

questions.solution:
(a)(i)(I) The convention for naming restriction enzymes is based on the organism from which they are isolated. EcoR I is named as follows: 'E' stands for the genus Escherichia; 'co' stands for the species coli; 'R' refers to the specific strain RY13 from which it was first isolated; and 'I' indicates that it was the first restriction enzyme isolated from this strain. This systematic naming helps scientists identify the source organism and the order of discovery of the enzyme.

(a)(i)(II) The recognition site of EcoR I is a palindromic sequence:
5'—G A A T T C—3'
3'—C T T A A G—5'
EcoR I cuts between G and A on both strands, producing staggered cuts.

(a)(ii) The overhanging single-stranded stretches produced by restriction enzymes that cut DNA in a staggered manner are called sticky ends (or cohesive ends). Their role in rDNA formation is as follows: When two different DNA molecules are cut with the same restriction enzyme, they produce complementary sticky ends. These complementary sticky ends can base-pair with each other when two DNA fragments are brought together — for example, a gene of interest and a plasmid vector cut with the same enzyme. The hydrogen bonding between complementary sticky ends holds the two fragments in place, and DNA ligase then forms covalent phosphodiester bonds to permanently join them, creating a stable recombinant DNA molecule.

OR
(b)(i) Insertional inactivation is used to detect recombinant DNA using the vector pBR322, which contains two antibiotic resistance genes — ampicillin resistance (amp^r) and tetracycline resistance (tet^r). When a foreign DNA fragment is inserted into the BamH I site within the tet^r gene, it disrupts and inactivates the tetracycline resistance gene. Recombinant bacteria are identified by plating on ampicillin medium (all transformants grow, since amp^r is intact) and then replica plating on tetracycline medium. Colonies that grow on ampicillin but not on tetracycline are the recombinants — they contain the foreign DNA insert that has disrupted tet^r. Colonies that grow on both media are non-recombinants.

(b)(ii) The Ti (tumour-inducing) plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens is the commonly used vector for transferring genes into plant cells.

(b)(iii) The Ti plasmid carries a region called T-DNA (transfer DNA) which integrates into the plant cell's nuclear genome. Once integrated, the T-DNA contains genes that cause the plant cell to overproduce plant growth hormones such as auxins and cytokinins. This uncontrolled hormonal production leads to unregulated cell proliferation, forming a tumour known as crown gall. When used as a vector for plant genetic engineering, the tumour-causing genes on T-DNA are disarmed (removed) and replaced with the desired foreign gene, while retaining the ability to integrate into the plant genome.

questions.text_english:
(a) Study the flow chart given below. Name the hormones involved at each stage and explain their functions.
Hypothalamus → Pituitary → Ovary → Pregnancy
OR
(b) (i) Draw a diagram of L.S. of maize grain and label its any six parts.
(ii) Differentiate between perisperm and endosperm giving one example of each.

key_points: Hypothalamus releases GnRH (Gonadotropin Releasing Hormone) which stimulates the anterior pituitary.
Pituitary releases FSH and LH: FSH stimulates follicle development and oestrogen secretion; LH surge triggers ovulation and corpus luteum formation.
Ovary releases oestrogen (follicular phase, stimulates endometrium) and progesterone (luteal phase, maintains endometrium for implantation).
During pregnancy: hCG (from placenta) maintains corpus luteum; placenta produces oestrogen, progesterone, and hPL to maintain pregnancy.

OR (b)(ii): Perisperm is residual nucellus tissue (persistent nucellus) that stores food in the seed; example: black pepper, beet. Endosperm is a triploid (3n) nutritive tissue formed from triple fusion; example: coconut, maize.

questions.solution:
(a) Hypothalamus: The hypothalamus secretes GnRH (Gonadotropin Releasing Hormone), which acts on the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland to stimulate the release of gonadotropins.

Pituitary: In response to GnRH, the anterior pituitary secretes two hormones — FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) and LH (Luteinising Hormone). FSH stimulates the growth and maturation of ovarian follicles and also promotes the secretion of oestrogen by the growing follicle. LH stimulates the final maturation of the follicle and triggers ovulation (release of the egg). After ovulation, LH causes the ruptured follicle to transform into the corpus luteum.

Ovary: The developing follicle secretes oestrogen, which causes proliferation of the uterine endometrium and prepares the female reproductive system for fertilisation. After ovulation, the corpus luteum secretes progesterone, which maintains and thickens the endometrium to receive the implanting embryo and supports early pregnancy.

Pregnancy: If fertilisation and implantation occur, the developing placenta secretes hCG (human Chorionic Gonadotropin), which prevents degeneration of the corpus luteum and maintains its progesterone and oestrogen secretion during early pregnancy. The placenta itself later becomes the main source of oestrogen, progesterone, and hPL (human Placental Lactogen), which together maintain the pregnancy, prepare mammary glands for lactation, and regulate foetal growth.

OR
(b)(i) A labelled L.S. of maize grain should show: Pericarp (fruit wall), Seed coat (testa), Endosperm (starchy), Aleurone layer, Scutellum (cotyledon), Coleoptile, Plumule, Radicle, Coleorhiza, Epiblast.

(b)(ii) Perisperm is the residual nutritive tissue derived from the nucellus (remains of the megasporangium wall) that persists in the mature seed. It is found in seeds where the nucellus is not completely consumed during development. Example: Black pepper (Piper nigrum) and beet. Endosperm is a triploid (3n) nutritive tissue formed as a result of triple fusion (one sperm nucleus + two polar nuclei) during double fertilisation in angiosperms. It provides nourishment to the developing embryo. Example: Coconut (the white kernel is the endosperm) and maize.

(a) Write the types and locations of the genes causing thalassemia in humans. State the cause and symptoms of the disease. How is sickle-cell anemia different from this disease?
OR
(b) (i) Enlist any four prime goals of the Human Genome Project (HGP).
(ii) List the two methodologies which were involved in the human genome project. Mention how they were used.
(iii) Expand 'YAC' and mention what it was used for.

key_points: Thalassemia: caused by autosomal recessive mutations in alpha-globin genes (chromosome 16) or beta-globin genes (chromosome 11).
Cause: reduced or absent synthesis of globin chains; leads to defective haemoglobin.
Symptoms: severe anaemia, splenomegaly, bone deformities, growth retardation.

Difference from sickle cell anaemia: Thalassemia involves reduced/absent globin production (quantitative defect); sickle cell involves a structural abnormality (qualitative defect — amino acid substitution).
OR (b): Four goals of HGP; two methodologies are EST (Expressed Sequence Tags) and Sequence Annotation; YAC = Yeast Artificial Chromosome, used for cloning large DNA fragments.

questions.solution:
(a) Thalassemia is an autosomal recessive genetic disorder. It is caused by mutations in the genes encoding the globin chains of haemoglobin. Alpha-thalassemia is caused by mutations or deletions in the alpha-globin genes located on chromosome 16. Beta-thalassemia is caused by mutations in the beta-globin gene located on chromosome 11. There are two copies of the alpha-globin gene per chromosome (four in total), and mutations in one, two, three, or all four copies lead to increasingly severe forms. The cause of thalassemia is the reduced or complete absence of synthesis of one type of globin chain, leading to the formation of abnormal, unstable haemoglobin molecules. The imbalance in globin chain production causes the red blood cells to be fragile and break down rapidly. The symptoms of thalassemia include severe haemolytic anaemia (low haemoglobin), enlargement of the spleen (splenomegaly) due to excessive destruction of red blood cells, skeletal deformities (especially facial and long bones) due to expansion of bone marrow, growth retardation, and dependence on frequent blood transfusions in severe cases (thalassemia major). How thalassemia differs from sickle cell anaemia: Sickle cell anaemia is a qualitative (structural) haemoglobin disorder — a single point mutation causes the substitution of glutamic acid by valine at the sixth position of the beta-globin chain, producing a structurally abnormal haemoglobin S. Thalassemia, on the other hand, is a quantitative disorder — the globin chain is normal in structure but is produced in insufficient amounts or not at all. Both are autosomal recessive conditions, but sickle cell anaemia shows co-dominance while thalassemia is strictly recessive.

OR
(b)(i) Four prime goals of the Human Genome Project were: (1) To identify all approximately 20,000–25,000 genes in human DNA. (2) To determine the sequences of the 3 billion chemical base pairs that make up human DNA. (3) To store this information in databases. (4) To develop tools for data analysis and to address the ethical, legal, and social issues arising from the project (ELSI).

(b)(ii) Two methodologies used in HGP: (1) Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) — this approach focused on identifying all genes that are expressed (transcribed into mRNA) in cells. Scientists created complementary DNA (cDNA) libraries from mRNA and sequenced the cDNA fragments to tag and identify expressed genes. (2) Sequence Annotation — the entire genomic DNA was sequenced using the shotgun sequencing approach and automated DNA sequencers. The sequences were then assembled and annotated using bioinformatics tools to identify gene locations and functions.

(b)(iii) YAC stands for Yeast Artificial Chromosome. In the HGP, YACs were used as cloning vectors because they could accommodate very large DNA inserts (up to hundreds of kilobases in size). They were used to clone large fragments of human genomic DNA, making it possible to sequence and map the entire human genome efficiently.
